body:
Could you try to use a string to the module instead of a function for `loadChildren`?

Also, the CLI is broken right now until https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/11387 is in and released.

When trying to pass in a string angular seems to try to lazy load although I'm using webpack with a single bundle. (with my setup this fails as it's missing System.JS I think) I don't need lazy loading (nor would I know how to setup my bundles correctly ;)) so using a function to load the module worked perfectly fine for me.

@choeller it fails because it uses `System.import()`, yes, but not because you're missing `SystemJS`. `SystemJS` is a library that implements a polyfill of `System.import()`, but normally webpack is able to detect calls to it and refactor the code to use an internal webpack-specific implementation. In the current RC6 the bug is that webpack is not smart enough to detect the call to `System.import()` and leave the code as is, resulting in a real call to a non-existant `System`. 

There are many ways to fix it, but there's only 2 ways that work with the CLI:
1. using a function that manually calls `System.import()`, similar to what @qdouble posted in his second example. You could also use the first one but it's more reliant on webpack and might require more typing.
2. use a string and the nightly build of Angular which has #11387 in it.

There is a few other solutions but they're way more complicated. The truth is, when Angular RC6+1 comes around with bug fixes that bug will be fixed in Angular. Until then, you're stuck with a manual solution, at least temporarily.

@hansl I'm a bit confused by your reply, it seems you are not specifically addressing the issue as it pertains to AOT. You said the export functions work are a solution, but they do not work properly in AOT mode. It compiles fine, but when you actually navigate to the route it gives the `t.create is not a function error`. 

I'm using the latest nightly builds by the way.
That's because Lazy Loading changes with AoT. You're not loading a module anymore, but a module factory.

@hansl so the solution would be that we have to point to somewhere different when the module is loaded lazily? Like in JIT it'd point to `LazyModule` and in AOT we'd set it to point to `LazyModuleNgFactory`? Or is there some other workaround we need to implement?

@hansl Okay, I got what you are saying now...if I point directly to the ngc generated factory, it lazy loads fine. Seems that unless you have a plugin that knows where your tsconfig output is going and that can parse your existing module, it could be a bit tedious to set both...but assuming you don't have a boat load of lazy loaded modules, doing it manually isn't torture I suppose.

If you use a string, the module loader will inject an `ngfactory` in the string before calling system.import. That's why you don't need to change anything in that case.

One way we've been doing AoT is by running the ngc tool ourselves and then using the cli to compile. Rob Wormald should be close to be done with integrating AoT in the CLI. That will also include code to support lazy loading.

@hansl could you give me an example of `return System.import('./features/lazy').then((r: any) => r.LazyModule);` into a valid string? I'm having issues getting it to work, not quite sure how it's supposed to look.
